verdicts.flaw_description: A concurrent alternative cause reaches every unit: "Each shop moved its machines to a coated carbide insert grade that quarter, and every logged run was cut on one of those machines." A new insert grade directly changes cutting speed on titanium, so the 4-7 minute reductions are equally explained by the insert change rather than the coolant.

The outcome is measured on a narrower population than the claim: "Rates cover the patients whose whole stay ran under the protocol, and a quarter of each ward's patients had spells outside the protocol." The 6-11 percent drops are per-protocol figures that drop 25 percent of patients (plausibly the longer-stay, higher-risk ones), while the claim is about ward infection rates as a whole.

The figures cover only part of the population the claim is about: "Figures cover the orders rung up at the new prices, and about a fifth of each line's orders were rung up at the old prices." Roughly 20 percent of current orders are excluded while the month-earlier baseline is the full line, so the 4-7 percent gap can reflect which orders got the new price rather than the pricing change raising revenue per order.

Two of the four cases have the outcome measured before treatment started: cohort One "started 4 April; by 29 March resting heart rate ran 5 bpm below" and cohort Three "started 5 October; by 30 September ... 6 bpm below." A drop recorded a week before enrolment cannot have been produced by the app.
